description_full: Spotify Technology S.A., together with its subsidiaries, provides audio streaming subscription services worldwide. It operates in two segments, Premium and Ad-Supported. The Premium segment offers online and offline streaming access to its catalog of music and podcasts, including video, lossless music, and audiobooks in select markets through subscription offerings primarily sold directly to end users and partners. The Ad-Supported segment provides limited on-demand online access to its catalog of music and online and offline access to its catalog of podcasts on computers, tablets, mobile devices, and other smart devices. The company also offers sales, distribution and marketing, contract research and development, and customer and other support services. Spotify Technology S.A. was incorporated in 2006 and is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden.

financial_summary: Spotify Technology S.A. is a large-cap communication services business with a $118.6B market cap on $18.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $3.2B in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 8.3×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 23% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
